course_name_and_code: Fundamentals in AI and Optimization Techniques (DVAE23)
positive_summary: Discussions around the subject and varied teaching methods were highly valued by the students
The examination tasks are considered to have been well connected to the content of the teaching
Students felt that the course forced them to allocate time and that they generally prepared well
critique_summary: The feedback provided was not perceived to be helpful enough in the later evaluations
The NPS result (Net Promoter Score) dropped drastically from +100 to strongly negative figures (-66.67 and -80)
Student engagement/involvement in lectures and seminars decreased and the course structure's support functions deteriorated slightly
trend_over_time: The course started in 2023 with very good results and high satisfaction. During 2024, grades and satisfaction dropped sharply (partly explained by the course coordinator being on sick leave)...

student_quotes.quote: The lab sessions were genuinely the best part. We got to apply theory straight away and the TAs were always there to help.
I loved how the lectures connected directly to real industry problems. It made studying feel relevant rather than just abstract theory.
The exam came out of nowhere — the practice questions didn't really match the actual difficulty. More alignment there would help a lot.
Workload was brutal in weeks 4 and 5. Three deadlines at the same time felt unmanageable.
Yes, definitely recommend — but only if you are ready for a serious time commitment.

teacher_reflection: The course ran well overall and the statistical scores confirm a solid foundation. The drop in workload satisfaction was expected given that we introduced a new compulsory group project this term. Going forward, I plan to stagger the deadlines more evenly. The feedback quality issue is noted — I will provide more detailed rubrics for lab submissions in the next iteration.
